title: Intracortical speech neuroprosthesis restores conversation for a man with ALS (UC Davis, BrainGate2)
summary: Four 64-electrode arrays and a neural decoder let Casey Harrell converse. Selected conversation sessions had a 3.7% word error rate; a later report describes 1.96 million words at home.
account: At the University of California Davis, a 45-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and severe dysarthria took part in the BrainGate2 trial (NCT00912041). Press identify him as Casey Harrell. Four 64-electrode arrays were implanted in his left precentral gyrus in July 2023. From August 2023, a decoder predicting phonemes every 80 ms, with language models over a 125,000-word vocabulary, converted his attempted speech to text. Accuracy was 99.6% with a 50-word vocabulary on day one and 90.2% with the full vocabulary on day two. Prompted-speech accuracy reached 97.5%. Harrell used the system for 248.3 hours of conversation over 8.4 months; selected conversation sessions had a 3.7% word error rate. The paper gives only the month for the first session, so 1 August 2023 is used.
purpose: Built to restore communication by decoding attempted speech from intracortical activity into text. Conversational communication was the intended benefit and is what occurred.
system: UC Davis intracortical speech neuroprosthesis (BrainGate2 trial)
model_version: Four 64-electrode microelectrode arrays (256 electrodes) in the left precentral gyrus; phoneme decoder with an openly available language model assembling phonemes into words and two further open-source language models producing the sentence, over a 125,000-word vocabulary
developer: UC Davis Neuroprosthetics Lab (Brandman, Stavisky) with the BrainGate consortium

ratings.reason: Life-changing benefit to one identifiable person: conversational communication with family and colleagues was restored. The 2026 follow-up documents over 3,800 hours of unsupervised home use, nearly two million words and continued full-time employment.

ai_role.statement: A neural-network decoder (phoneme prediction every 80 ms) combined with language models is the mechanism converting attempted speech into text. The benefit is attributable to the decoding system, with surgery and arrays as enabling hardware.

produced_by: Preserved speech-motor cortical activity during attempted speech despite severe dysarthria
256-electrode intracortical recording in the ventral precentral gyrus

must_hold: Array signal quality remains stable over months to years

fields.account: At the University of California Davis, a 45-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and severe dysarthria took part in the BrainGate2 trial (NCT00912041). Press identify him as Casey Harrell. Four 64-electrode arrays were implanted in his left precentral gyrus in July 2023. From August 2023, a decoder predicting phonemes every 80 ms, with language models over a 125,000-word vocabulary, converted his attempted speech to text. Accuracy was 99.6% with a 50-word vocabulary on day one and 90.2% with the full vocabulary on day two. Prompted-speech accuracy reached 97.5%. Harrell used the system for 248.3 hours of conversation over 8.4 months; selected conversation sessions had a 3.7% word error rate. The paper gives only the month for the first session, so 1 August 2023 is used.
